std_none.label: Current (as is)
std_none.note: The current-data fits from the factor page: standard factor model, COVID months kept.

cens_none.label: COVID censored
cens_none.note: Standard factor model; the five COVID months (Mar–Jul 2020) are dropped before the regime models are fitted (the chart skips them).

std_90.label: + 1990-style recession
std_90.note: Real data to Aug 2026 plus a SIMULATED mild recession shaped like 1990–91, starting Oct 2026, followed by the recovery and one more year of expansion to Feb 2030 (orange region; not real data). Standard factor model, COVID months kept.

extra_cols.label: Pr in new recession
extra_cols.tip: Mean Pr(low regime) over the 8 simulated recession months

extra_cols.label: Detection lag (months)
extra_cols.tip: Months from the first simulated recession month until Pr(low) reaches 50% (smoothed probabilities, so this is an in-sample not a real-time lag)

extra_cols.label: False alarms
extra_cols.tip: Share of the other simulated-period months (before and after the recession) with Pr(low) of 50% or more

extra_cols.label: AUC, new period
extra_cols.tip: AUC of Pr(low) against the recession indicator over the simulated period only

extra_cols.label: Real-time lag, ≥50% (months)
extra_cols.tip: Pseudo-real-time (refit on data up to each month): months from the first simulated recession month until the real-time Pr(low) reaches 50%

extra_cols.label: Real-time signal lag (3 mo ≥80%)
extra_cols.tip: Months until three consecutive real-time probabilities are all 80% or more (Piger's recession signal); the lag is measured at the third month

extra_cols.label: Real-time false alarms
extra_cols.tip: Share of the evaluated non-recession months from Sep 2026 on (the first month, the recovery) whose real-time Pr(low) is 50% or more
